entries.clue: Contemplate cycling with fast-running Australians (4)

indicatorNotes.cycling: the letters go round like a wheel: the last one comes to the front

blocks.note: to muse is to contemplate; its last letter is about to ride round to the front

annotation.surface: Someone lost in thought while jogging alongside a pack of speedy Aussies.
annotation.walkthrough: The Australians are birds, not athletes: emus are flightless but can sprint at around 50 km/h.
annotation.definitionFit: Emus are Australian birds that cannot fly but run very fast.

entries.clue: Man perhaps is left in addition (6)

annotation.surface: A remark that a man is surplus to requirements, left over as an extra.
annotation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland; the capital M is hidden at the start of the sentence. 'Perhaps' flags it as one example of an island.
annotation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so Man is an example of the answer.

entries.clue: Composition of Paganini in support of French perfume (10)

indicatorNotes.Composition of: composing the letters puts them into a new arrangement
indicatorNotes.in support of: in a down clue, the supporting piece sits beneath the other

annotation.surface: A piece by the violinist Paganini written to promote a French scent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Composition' pretends to mean a piece of music, apt for Paganini, but it tells you to rearrange his name, which then goes under FR.
annotation.definitionFit: Frangipani is a perfume made from, or imitating, the scent of the plumeria flower.

entries.clue: Move two men, extracting unit from Spanish region (6)

indicatorNotes.extracting: taking something out of the word that follows

annotation.surface: An order to relocate two workers out of a province of Spain.
annotation.walkthrough: In chess, castling is the one move that shifts two pieces at once, king and rook; chess pieces are often called men, and this puzzle runs on them.
annotation.definitionFit: To castle in chess is to move king and rook together in a single turn.

entries.clue: Pay for drink that holds water (6,2)

blocks.note: to stand someone a drink is to pay for it

annotation.surface: Buying a drink, perhaps a glass of water, for someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Holds water' has nothing to do with a glass: an argument that holds water is sound, just as one that stands up is.
annotation.definitionFit: An argument that holds water survives scrutiny; so does one that stands up.

entries.clue: Boatman: extremely lithe and fit (4)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the extremes, the first and last letters

blocks.note: AB, the abbreviation for a rated seaman, a sailor
L and E, the ends of 'lithe'

annotation.surface: The setter, Boatman, boasting of being supple and in good shape.
annotation.walkthrough: Boatman is this setter's pseudonym, so the clue looks like a boast, but here it means any sailor: AB, an able seaman.
annotation.definitionFit: Able and fit both mean capable or suitable, as in fit or able for work.

entries.clue: Compilation edited to remove letters from man, a party animal (8)

indicatorNotes.edited: editing reworks the text, so the remaining letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.to remove letters from: the letters of the word that follows are taken out

blocks.note: M, A and N are removed, leaving COPILTIO

annotation.surface: An album being cut down to leave out a man who loves a good party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party animal' suggests a reveller, but the party is political: a politico lives for party politics.
annotation.definitionFit: A politico is a person devoted to party politics, so a creature of the party.

entries.clue: 2 keys used in pieces (4)

indicatorNotes.used in pieces: the letters are broken apart and put back together differently

annotation.walkthrough: '2' points to the answer to 2 down, ISLAND; Skye is a Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides. The keys pretend to be a piano's.
annotation.definitionFit: Skye is an island off the west coast of Scotland.

entries.clue: Centrism in turmoil about one troublemaker (9)

indicatorNotes.in turmoil: turmoil throws the letters into disorder
indicatorNotes.about: the rearranged letters go round the next piece

annotation.surface: The political centre ground in chaos over a single agitator.
annotation.walkthrough: The rearranged CENTRISM goes around A, which sits between MISCRE and NT.
annotation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer, someone who causes trouble.

entries.clue: Second man gets permit … (5)

blocks.note: B is the second letter or grade
a rook is a chess man

annotation.surface: A deputy obtains a licence, the story running on into the next clue.
annotation.walkthrough: Chess pieces are called men, the puzzle's running joke. The ellipsis links this to 11 across, which reads as the sentence's end.
annotation.definitionFit: To brook something is to permit or tolerate it, usually in 'brook no argument'.

entries.clue: … to get second man (5)

blocks.note: s = second, the unit of time
a pawn is a chess man

annotation.surface: Continuing 10 across: a deputy gets permission to father another man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get' in the old sense of beget, to father offspring. 'Second' is S here, not the B of 10 across.
annotation.definitionFit: To get, in the old sense of beget, is to produce offspring, which is to spawn.

entries.clue: Orange fury stops pointed article (9)

indicatorNotes.stops: the first piece plugs the second, like a stopper in a bottle

blocks.note: a tine is a prong, as on a fork

annotation.surface: Someone's orange rage halts a sharp object.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests A or THE, but here it is a thing with a point: a fork's tine. 'Stops' reads as halting, but here it means plugging a gap.
annotation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small orange, and the word is also the colour.

entries.clue: Drug laws in Spain (7)

blocks.note: a code is a body of laws
E is Spain's international vehicle code

annotation.surface: The rules on narcotics in Spain.
annotation.walkthrough: E for Spain comes from the country letters on cars (España). The surface reads as drug laws, but 'laws' and 'Drug' are separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Codeine is a painkilling drug derived from opium.

entries.clue: Confirm payment from America (5)

annotation.surface: Verifying that money has come in from the United States.
annotation.walkthrough: British English writes the payment slip as cheque; the American spelling matches the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A check is the American form of a cheque, a written order to pay money.

entries.clue: Perhaps Paddington is still not finished – no limits for his creator (7)

indicatorNotes.not finished: the word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.no limits for: the first and last letters are dropped

blocks.note: STATIC, still, without its final C
Michael BOND wrote the Paddington books; without its ends, BOND gives ON

annotation.surface: Paddington Bear still unfinished, and his author left without bounds.
annotation.walkthrough: Paddington is the bear named after the London railway station where he was found; the definition is the station, while the bear's author Michael Bond supplies the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Paddington is a major London railway station, so one example of a station.

entries.clue: Poses on one foot off base in square-dancing (10)

indicatorNotes.off: base knocked off, out of its order
indicatorNotes.in: the first letters are placed within the next word
indicatorNotes.dancing: dancers never stay in one place, so the letters step into a new order

annotation.surface: A square dancer balancing on one leg and slipping out of position.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Square-dancing' looks like one hyphenated word, but it splits into fodder SQUARE and indicator 'dancing'.
annotation.definitionFit: An arabesque is a ballet position on one leg, the other stretched out behind.

entries.clue: Dark man in audience (5)

indicatorNotes.in audience: an audience hears the word rather than reading it

blocks.note: a knight is a chess man, and sounds the same

annotation.surface: A sinister figure seated among the spectators.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dark' reads as an adjective in the surface but is the noun: after dark means after nightfall.
annotation.definitionFit: Dark as a noun means night, as in 'home before dark'.

entries.clue: A piece of text? Rather more (5)

indicatorNotes.A piece of: the answer is a piece cut out of the words that follow

annotation.surface: Someone asking for a snippet of writing and being told it is rather more than that.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark breaks the surface in two, but the answer runs straight across it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something extra is over and above, as in 'extra time' or 'more time'.

entries.clue: Seminar on support for retort (4,4)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

annotation.surface: A seminar on how to give lip, or on supporting a comeback.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retort' is the verb, to answer back rudely, which is what talk back means.
annotation.definitionFit: To talk back is to answer insolently, which is to retort.

entries.clue: Dance piece, twice released (3)

indicatorNotes.released: the named letters are let go from the word

blocks.note: a bishop is a chess piece
bis is Latin for twice; these letters are dropped

annotation.surface: A dance number that has been put out on two occasions.
annotation.walkthrough: BIS, twice, is used in music and in numbering (flat 3 bis). With it released, BISHOP leaves HOP, an informal word for a dance.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal, rather dated word for a social dance, as in the American sock hop of the 1950s.

entries.clue: Sound, something that trumpeters aim for in the main (4,4)

indicatorNotes.Sound: what follows is a spoken sound, spelt another way

blocks.note: top Cs, the notes trumpeters strive to hit

annotation.surface: A trumpeter lined up at sea, aiming for top notes.
annotation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the open ocean, as in the Spanish Main.
annotation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic term for the open sea, which is the high seas.

entries.clue: Devious man and go-between (5)

indicatorNotes.Devious: devious means going by a winding route, so the letters wander

annotation.surface: A cunning man acting as an intermediary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go-between' looks like one word, a messenger, but splits: GO is fodder and 'between' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Among and between both mean in the midst of, as in 'shared among friends'.

entries.clue: Man admits evil murder? (7)

indicatorNotes.admits: lets something in, so the second piece goes inside

blocks.note: the king is a chess man
ill = evil, as in ill deeds; placed inside KING

annotation.surface: A man confesses to a wicked murder.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a confession; the question mark signals that 'Man' is a chess piece rather than a suspect.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: the act of taking a life unlawfully, as in 'a gangland killing'.

entries.clue: Host transmitted in advance? (7)

annotation.surface: A television host whose show was broadcast ahead of time.
annotation.walkthrough: Host is the verb: to present a programme. The pieces go in reverse order to the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Broadcasting sense: the person fronting a programme introduces it, so hosting and presenting are the same job.

entries.clue: Boatman in online article on southern states (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the first piece goes inside the next
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, the upper piece rests on the one below

blocks.note: a post is an item published online
the setter, Boatman, is I; placed inside POST

annotation.surface: The setter featured in an internet piece about the American South.
annotation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter, so he is I. 'Southern states' is a trap: the definition is just 'states', a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To posit is to state or put forward as fact.

entries.clue: Rues turning down top to waders (6)

indicatorNotes.turning down top: declining the top, which in a down clue is the first letter

blocks.note: rues = regrets, verb; drop the R

annotation.surface: Someone sorry for rejecting a top that goes with their waders.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turning down' reads as folding a waistband, but means refusing: the top letter R is turned away.
annotation.definitionFit: Egrets are herons that wade in shallow water, so waders.

entries.clue: Rouses rabble with lie after naked lie, concealing dollars to gain heart of Essex (9)

indicatorNotes.after: the second lie comes after the first
indicatorNotes.concealing: the letters go round the next piece, hiding it
indicatorNotes.to gain: adds the next piece on the end
indicatorNotes.heart of: the heart sits in the middle of the body, so take the word's central letter

blocks.note: used as printed; it goes round the S
$ looks like S; LIE conceals it as LISE

annotation.surface: A rabble-rouser telling lie upon lie, pocketing cash to win over Essex.
annotation.walkthrough: The chain builds I + LIE, then puts S inside the LIE to get LISE, then tacks on S. Essex is a county east of London.
annotation.definitionFit: To mobilise people is to rouse them into action.

entries.clue: Tea with a friend (4)

blocks.note: maté, the South American herbal tea
a pal, in British and Australian slang

annotation.surface: Having a cup of tea with a pal.
annotation.walkthrough: Maté is a caffeinated infusion drunk in Argentina and Uruguay; crosswords drop the accent.
annotation.definitionFit: Maté is a tea made from the leaves of a South American holly; a mate is a friend.

entries.clue: Behind time getting up – and the rest (4)

indicatorNotes.getting up: in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom up

blocks.note: et al. = and the rest, from the Latin et alii

annotation.surface: Someone oversleeping, and everyone else too.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a late riser, and the reversed ET AL makes LATE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a train running behind time is running late.

entries.clue: Holy text with God appearing where there is need essentially in Man (5)

indicatorNotes.appearing where there is: the new piece takes the place of the named letters

blocks.note: the queen is a chess man
the middle letters of nEEd, which are replaced
Ra, the Egyptian sun god, takes the place of EE

annotation.surface: Scripture bringing God where he is needed in mankind.
annotation.walkthrough: Swapping EE in QUEEN for RA gives QU-RA-N. The capital on 'Man' suggests the Isle of Man, but it is a chess piece again.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Muslims hold it to be the word of God revealed to Muhammad, Islam's sacred scripture.

entries.clue: Take shape (4)

blocks.note: take in the sense of steal, in British slang

annotation.surface: An instruction to form or develop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take shape' reads as one phrase but splits in two. Nick is British slang for steal, and 'in good nick' means in good shape.
annotation.definitionFit: Nick means steal (take) and, as a noun, condition (shape).

entries.clue: Tips to transform any communication instantly: try without words (5)

indicatorNotes.Tips: the tips of the words are their first letters

blocks.clueFragment: to transform any communication instantly: try

annotation.surface: Advice for translating a message instantly: try doing it without speaking.
annotation.walkthrough: The first letters start with 'to', a word that looks like a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood without being spoken.

entries.clue: Accurately depicted Gaul, Athens and Utica for Discovery (9)

indicatorNotes.Discovery: read as dis-cover-y: take off the covers, the outer letters

annotation.surface: A faithful portrayal of three ancient places in a history documentary.
annotation.walkthrough: Discovery pretends to be a TV channel, but read it as dis-covering: each place name loses its outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Something authentic is true to life, accurately depicted.
